A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 15-page paper, including Appendices A–C. All manuscript text matches except the first-page arXiv version/date stamp; rendered pages 2–15 are identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original GPT-4o, Llama 3.1 and o3 experiments on coreference resolution and ambiguity detection, plus AmbiEnt evaluations (Tables 8 and 10–12). These model results are distinct from the reused human annotations.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original model experiments and outcomes, including the main results and the category analyses in Appendices A–C.

M1.justification: The prompting procedures and response mappings are identical, including REFLECT, BASIC, CoT, WSC, WSC-1sh and the five ambiguity-aware variants (Tables 2, 7 and 9).

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same English coreference and ambiguity-detection tasks using AmbiCoref and the same entailment task using AmbiEnt. Sentence categories and ambiguous/unambiguous coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments: the same GPT-4o and Llama 3.1 prompt comparisons, human reference judgments, and o3 evaluations appear in Tables 8 and 10–12.

E3.justification: Both retain 1,930 AmbiCoref sentences, 62 AmbiEnt pairs, the same model configurations and prompting conditions, and identical strict/near accuracy and Correct-Unamb/Detect-Ambig metrics.

E4.justification: Response-consistency analysis, gender comparisons, explanation–accuracy associations and category-specific investigations are unchanged (Section 4 and Appendices A–C). No ablation or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Section 3.2 retains the same three-run description for GPT-4o and Llama 3.1. The chi-square tests and p-value reporting in Appendix A and Table 13 are identical.

E6.justification: All numerical results and reported findings match, including Tables 3–6, 8 and 10–14 and Figures 2–7. For example, Table 10 retains GPT-4o Ambi-Wait detection of 99.55% and correctness of 5.23%.

T1.justification: Response-label and metric definitions are unchanged. Neither version adds, removes or revises a formal assumption, theorem, proof or mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same CORRECT-DETECT trade-off claim and claims about differences between human and model ambiguity sensitivity. Contribution scope and novelty claims are identical.

C2.justification: Both retain the training-incentive hypothesis in Section 8, the generalization qualifications in Section 7, and limitations concerning model coverage, English-only data and restricted sentence contexts. Appendix interpretations also match.

D1.justification: Model identifiers, complete prompt templates and AmbiEnt filtering instructions are identical. No implementation, reproducibility or code/data access information is added, removed or revised.

R1.justification: Section 2, the reference list and discussions connecting the findings to prior research are identical. No cited work or substantive research-positioning statement changes.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv margin stamp changes from v1 dated 17 September 2025 to v2 dated 21 October 2025. Manuscript wording, headings, terminology and organization otherwise remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–14 retain identical content, captions, formatting and placement. Page layouts match; the first-page stamp wording change does not alter the layout.

improvement.justification: v2 preserves the complete scientific content, results, interpretations, limitations and appendix material of v1. The updated version/date stamp and embedded publication metadata do not meaningfully change the paper's evidential strength, clarity or reproducibility.
